overview: This was the starting point for the Windows Server lab environment. I used a resource-constrained VMware VM to build a domain controller that later exercises could use for directory services and name resolution.

steps.title: Provision the server VM
steps.description: I created the VM using a manual installation workflow so I could choose the guest edition and hardware settings. The initial lab used two vCPUs, 2 GB RAM and a 20 GB virtual disk.

steps.title: Install Windows Server and inspect the baseline
steps.description: I installed the Desktop Experience edition and reviewed Server Manager while the machine was still in a workgroup.

steps.title: Rename the server
steps.description: I changed the generated computer name to DC01 before promotion so later configuration and management tools would identify its role clearly.

steps.title: Install VMware Tools and restart
steps.description: I installed the guest integration tools and combined the required restart with the pending computer-name change.

steps.title: Install the AD DS role
steps.description: I selected Active Directory Domain Services in Add Roles and Features, together with the associated directory and Group Policy management tools.

steps.title: Configure a new forest
steps.description: I launched the promotion wizard and selected Add a new forest for the isolated lab namespace. I configured the domain controller options and recovery access without publishing the credential values.

steps.title: Review prerequisites and promote DC01
steps.description: I checked the prerequisite results, reviewed the DNS delegation warning in the context of the isolated namespace, and proceeded with promotion and its restart.

steps.title: Set static IPv4 and DNS
steps.description: As recorded in my notes, I then set the server’s static private address and pointed preferred DNS at its own DNS service. Preparing static addressing before promotion is the preferable sequence for a repeat deployment.

steps.title: Inspect the directory and DNS result
steps.description: I reviewed the directory services, SYSVOL and DNS records described in the report to confirm that the standalone server had become the lab domain controller.

checks.title: Role and promotion prerequisites
checks.description: The screenshots show the AD DS role selection and passing promotion prerequisite checks.

checks.title: Static network settings
checks.description: The IPv4 properties screenshot shows static addressing and a self-referencing DNS setting.

checks.title: Directory initialization
checks.description: The notes describe reviewing the directory database, SYSVOL and DNS service records after promotion.

lessons: Installing the AD DS role and promoting a domain controller are separate operations.
DNS is a dependency for directory discovery and domain authentication.
A small VM can support a learning exercise, but its resource allocation is not a production sizing recommendation.
scope: The 20 GB disk was a constrained training allocation, below Microsoft’s published 32 GB installation baseline. I do not present it as a supported capacity recommendation or a fully hardened directory deployment.
